title: Fictional worked sample: conflicting workshop notes
text: **Record:** `distillation-record-v1`, reviewed project record. The synthetic exercise belongs to Maya's proposed thirty-minute Fieldwork workshop. It is not customer evidence or an observed learning result. **Future use:** Explain and test how action-list practice handles supplied deadline statements that conflict without an established supersession relationship. **Source A, passage 1:** “The group agreed that the facilitator will circulate the revised action list on Thursday.” **Source B, passage 1:** “The group agreed that the facilitator will circulate the revised action list on Friday.” These two short passages are the complete synthetic input for this example. No authorized clarification, reliable revision order, or superseding statement is supplied. Labels A and B identify passages; their order does not establish authority. Entry Statement Kind Support / limit Reviewed treatment C11-01 Source A states the facilitator will circulate the revised action list on Thursday. Source claim A, passage 1; synthetic statement, not proof of a real commitment. Retain faithfully. C11-02 Source B states the same action and owner with Friday as deadline. Source claim B, passage 1; no evidence it supersedes A. Retain faithfully. U11-01 The applicable deadline is unresolved in the supplied packet. Conclusion about available evidence A/B conflict; no supplied resolution. Retain with both links. D11-01 Keep the shared action and owner, show both deadline claims, and request clarification before presenting one as confirmed. Approved design decision Addresses the specific ambiguity while preserving established shared content. Add to the practice instructions after review. R11-01 Friday was confirmed when the schedule was clarified. Unsupported candidate claim No clarification exists in the input. Reject; keep only as a labeled failure example if useful. **Rationale:** Selecting Friday would invent supersession. Removing the whole action would lose content consistent across the inputs. The approved response preserves what agrees and locates uncertainty specifically in the deadline. **Change type:** Correct the candidate account's unsupported confirmation claim. No new real-world deadline decision is created. **Approval:** Maya approves the repaired project record and the bounded conflict-handling instruction. She approves neither Thursday nor Friday as the applicable deadline. The scope is representation of this kind of supplied ambiguity in the synthetic workshop practice. **Save route:** Save the reviewed record in the Fieldwork project workspace. Save the approved revision as `instructions-v3` and update the existing selector in `learning-loop-v1`; do not create another selector in this record. Link the explanatory `action-list-rule-rationale-v1` to this case. The general `commitment-evidence-principle-v1` can remain unchanged because it already expresses the relevant broad distinction.

title: Current instruction: instructions-v3
text: This is authored teaching material for the fictional case, not a transcript of a real model run. It extends the literal v2 instruction with the reviewed conflict-handling boundary. For the two passages above, source references can be `A:1` and `B:1`. Labels and document order do not establish which deadline applies. Whether an explicitly authorized later amendment would justify supersession is a further inquiry, not a result established by this practice case. **Stored-state check:** Reopen the saved record from the project index, inspect both source claims and the unresolved status, follow the current instruction pointer, and confirm the rejected Friday confirmation stays labeled rejected in retained history. An assistant saying “saved” is not this check.

title: Fresh-use specimen and regression check
text: Use the current instructions-v3 above. These are constructed teaching inputs and expected contrasts, not actual execution results. Keep the expected output separate when running your own attempt. **Expected specimen:** Status Action Owner Timing Evidence Agreed Circulate the revised action list Facilitator Tuesday in C:1; Wednesday in D:1; applicable date unresolved C:1 and D:1 **Clarification:** Which deadline applies? Both sources agree about the action and owner, but the supplied material does not settle the date. **Reject these candidates:** “Friday is confirmed” copies an earlier answer whose date does not occur here. “Wednesday is confirmed because D follows C” invents supersession. A candidate listing “Thursday/Friday unresolved” has preserved the idea of conflict but failed to apply it to the actual new input. **Earlier-owner regression input:** “E:1 The group agreed to shorten the opening discussion. No owner or deadline was assigned.” Status Action Owner Timing Evidence Agreed Shorten the opening discussion Unspecified Unspecified E:1 This expected row keeps an established agreement visible without inventing an assignment. Reject a response that drops it because ownership is missing or copies “facilitator” from the unrelated deadline examples. For your actual checks, record the input, supplied instruction version, first output, review, and any repair. The expected specimens above make comparison possible; they do not supply your observed result. **Interpretation:** These small synthetic checks inspect particular behaviors. They do not establish a measured general reliability rate, actual learner improvement, market demand, or that a real deadline has been resolved.

title: Acceptance criteria
text: The future use and available source boundary are explicit. Consequential claims can be checked separately without losing their meaning. Source claims, inferences, decisions, and preferences retain their distinct status. Conflicting evidence remains visible unless an actual authorized resolution is supplied. Rationale explains a material choice and its limits; unsupported certainty is removed. Approval identifies the exact wording, scope, and destination. Reopened saved state matches the approved record; links and current pointers work. A fresh attempt applies the retained lesson and preserves relevant earlier corrections.

title: Common failure and repair
text: Failure Repair A hypothesis becomes a customer fact Restore its hypothesis status and link the evidence ledger; do not invent validation. Repeated assistant summaries look like independent support Trace them to the original source and count the support accurately. The latest-looking passage silently wins a conflict Check actual authority and supersession; retain the conflict when neither is established. A correction is recorded as though the world changed State whether the source, record, or authorized decision changed. A short summary loses the reason for the rule Restore the consequential rejected alternatives, scope, and source route. The assistant reports saving, but the next task sees an old version Open the destination and current selector; repair the actual write or pointer. Fresh attempt repeats the old example's answer Clarify the rule's meaning, use the changed input, and repeat the check. Keep rejected drafts outside authoritative memory unless their labeled history has a defined purpose. Retention and sharing continue to follow the charter.

title: Open extension
text: **Proposed new input:** A synthetic record would explicitly identify an authorized coordinator changing the worksheet deadline from Friday to Monday. Maya has not yet prepared and reviewed that complete case. **Existing counterexample to preserve:** Two source statements giving different dates without establishing an authorized change, as in Chapter 11, must remain an unresolved conflict. **Present decision:** Keep Chapter 11’s approved unresolved-conflict rule. Investigate what evidence would distinguish an authorized amendment and how its history should remain visible. Do not record that extension as tested merely because it appears in the map. **Review needed:** Inspect I3, D, and R, compare T1, T2, and T3, retain their distinctions, then prepare and review a separate case for the new condition.

title: A walk that answers the question
text: Start at P → E → I3, then follow its links to D and R. Follow the case relationships to T1, T2, and T3. Open the actual notes and outputs. The answer is: inspect the current instruction and review sheet, the migration diagnosis, the rationale, and the existing no-date, vague-date, and unresolved-conflict cases before approving a separate amendment-handling extension. The route identifies relevant dependencies. It does not settle what missing context would establish approval of the date change.

title: Deliberate failure and repair
text: **Broken relationship:** `T1 used I2`. Every file can still open, but the packet explicitly identifies I1 as the supplied instruction for run-01. The incorrect edge would attribute the flawed example to the wrong version. **Repair:** Change that historical edge to `T1 used I1`. Keep `E points to current I3`. Repeat the historical walk and the current-use walk; they must reach different versions. Explain the distinction in your own words.

title: Acceptance criteria
text: Every item resolves to an inspectable record or is explicitly marked missing. Each consequential relationship can be explained as a sentence supported by the underlying records. Current instructions and historical versions remain distinguishable. A question can be answered through the links without adding an unstated personal memory. The deliberate wrong-version relationship can be diagnosed and repaired from the supplied packet. A proposal, a synthetic specimen, and a reviewed decision retain their distinct statuses. The map can be copied as ordinary text or tables without losing its relationship verbs and source locations.

title: Common failures and repairs
text: **Everything is “related to” everything:** Replace vague edges with the operation they support. Remove a connection if it does not help answer a working question. **An old test points to the latest instruction:** Restore its actual historical version. If the supplied version is unknown, say so and design a fresh comparison instead of guessing. **A generated relationship invents support:** Open the cited passage. Reject or narrow the edge; do not let a polished summary alter the evidence's status. **Maintaining the map costs more than its use saves:** Reduce the number of items, use document-level links, and retain an ordinary index where it is sufficient.

title: Verdict ledger
text: Use with Chapter 13: The Memory Flywheel. Retain a judgment, verify its saved form, and check its appropriate use on another input. This is a book-developed practice record, not an official SSA-CMM assessment.

title: No-code instructions
text: Copy the blank record into an ordinary document. Use the current-instruction route you already maintain. Keep a proposed verdict in the project workspace until you have compared it with the actual input and output. Promote only the reviewed record, reopen its saved destination, and start a changed-input attempt from that route. A reviewer may use a document editor and a fresh AI conversation; no code, account integration, or autonomous write is required.

title: Blank reusable record
text: Decision and status are separate. A rewrite decision remains a record of that candidate even after a corrected candidate is accepted. Superseding a record changes its current applicability; it does not silently rewrite the original evidence.

title: Worked packet: fictional Fieldwork
text: All notes, outputs, decisions, and record excerpts below are **authored teaching specimens**. They are not transcripts of model runs, file-write receipts, learner observations, or customer evidence. The packet makes the method inspectable. Replace its specimens with your own saved work when performing the exercise. **Project:** Maya's proposed thirty-minute action-list workshop. The immediate task is preparing an example action list within the design materials; the final workshop brief remains `workshop-brief-v1`. **Existing project route:** Project index → the existing `learning-loop-v1` selector → current `instructions-v3`. `action-list-rule-rationale-v1` explains the rule and its history. The knowledge map links the relevant records. This packet does not create a second authority route. **New record:** `verdict-ledger-v1`, with verdict `V13-01`. In this self-contained teaching packet, the following section links represent the corresponding source, instruction, and output files.

title: Current instruction: worked excerpt
text: This task-specific summary recalls the relevant rules from the linked literal `instructions-v3`; that existing instruction remains authoritative. This represents the already-approved instruction. The new verdict enforces it; the instruction does not need another version merely because a new example is reviewed.

title: V13-01: reviewed verdict
text: **Judged object:** Output A, specifically its deadline. **Evidence:** Input A, lines A1–A2; current instruction. **Reviewer:** Maya, within the fictional case. **Decision:** Rewrite. **Reason:** Thursday is absent from the input, which supplies only “soon” and explicitly says no calendar date was agreed. The action and owner are supported and should remain. **Required correction:** Preserve the stated timing and identify the remaining lack of precision. Do not silently replace “soon” with a date or delete the supported action. **Reusable lesson:** Preserve the timing the source establishes. Do not supply unsupported precision. When a precise date is explicitly supplied, retain it; when claims conflict, preserve the conflict under the current instruction. **Scope:** Fieldwork's source-faithful action-list drafting and review. The verdict grants no authority to assign work, contact participants, invent source context, or resolve contradictory deadlines. **Reconsideration trigger:** A corrected source for this case, a changed instruction/authority contract, or evidence that the lesson mishandles a legitimate input. No arbitrary time expiry is assigned to the general evidence boundary. A new input still requires an applicability check. **Status:** Reviewed for the stated scope. Superseding evidence should receive a linked new review; preserve this record as a judgment of Input A and Output A.

title: Output A: reviewed correction
text: **Correction review:** Accept this constructed candidate for its stated design use. Each field is supported by the supplied notes, and the unresolved detail remains visible. This acceptance concerns the corrected output; the rewrite verdict on the original candidate remains in history.

title: Rejected reusable wording
text: Leave the deadline unknown. **Status: rejected as a general instruction.** It drops the stated “soon” information and would also erase the explicit Thursday in Input B. Do not include this sentence in the active instruction packet. It is retained here to explain the more precise wording in V13-01.

title: Saved record and verification target
text: The project's current pointer continues to select the existing instruction. The new verdict is linked as supporting judgment, with its object, evidence, reason, scope, status, and review trigger intact. The rationale and manual knowledge map point to it where it explains the requirement. For this packet, reopen V13-01, then follow its input and instruction links. Confirm that the record still includes the exception for a precise date explicitly supplied by the source. Follow the reviewed correction and compare its fields with A1–A2. For your actual project, perform that check by reopening the saved document through your normal project route. Record the destination and what you observed. If a practice copy contains the verdict while the normal route opens an older record, mark the save/use-route check failed and repair the destination or pointer before reuse. Do not report a verified write merely because the draft text exists in a conversation.

title: Input B: explicit timing
text: **Expected properties before drafting:** Keep the agreement, the facilitator, and Thursday. The source supports the timing; V13-01 prohibits invention, not dates. **Working packet supplied:** Current instruction, V13-01, and Input B. The rejected reusable wording remains historical and is not supplied as a command.

title: Output B: acceptable reuse specimen
text: **Review:** Accept this constructed response for the stated design use. It preserves supported precision rather than copying Input A's uncertainty. The source-to-claim relationship carries forward; the earlier output's content does not.

title: Output B: rejected overgeneralization
text: **Review:** Rewrite. B1 supplies Thursday; the candidate misstates V13-01's scope and erases supported information. The current instruction does not need a new date rule. Check which wording was supplied and whether rejected history was wrongly treated as current. If the correct packet was supplied, record a rule violation without inventing an unobserved cause.

title: Reuse record
text: **Prior correction:** `V13-01`, preserving source-supported timing without inventing precision. **Changed condition:** Input A has imprecise timing; Input B supplies a specific weekday. **Evidence:** The two literal Input B outputs above expose acceptable use and overgeneralization. They are contrasting authored examples, not a measured success/failure pair from a model. **Working consequence:** Retain the current instruction. Add the reviewed verdict and contrasting cases to its supporting rationale. Keep the rejected generalization visibly historical. Maya can incorporate the accepted action-list example in her practice materials after review; this establishes no learner effect. **Further boundary:** If two source passages disagree about the deadline without establishing supersession, retain the supported action and both claims, then request clarification under the existing conflict policy. Do not select Thursday merely because this example used it.

title: Acceptance and repair
text: The record is usable when a reviewer can inspect the judged object and evidence, understand the verdict's scope, find the verified saved record, and trace appropriate reuse in a changed input. Your own completed exercise must contain actual saved inputs/outputs and your observed checks, not just the supplied examples. Failure Repair Verdict says only “bad” or “better” Identify the exact unsupported claim or unmet criterion and its evidence A correct case repair becomes an overbroad rule Add a legitimate alternative the reusable wording must permit Verdict exists only in the editing session Reopen the approved destination through the normal project route Historical rejection becomes a current instruction Keep its status with its text and exclude it from active commands A new output violates an already-explicit rule Inspect the actual packet and conflicting examples before changing the rule Source changes but the verdict remains unquestioned Link a fresh review; identify whether the old case still applies A reviewed verdict turns out to be mistaken Mark it withdrawn with a correction link; inspect affected instructions and outputs, then verify the corrected route Review rejects a whole useful output for one unknown detail Preserve uncontested content and identify the specific clarification needed Ledger fills with duplicate discoveries Link recurring cases to the existing scoped judgment; add a new verdict when the decision changes Close the packet and explain why “soon,” Thursday, and contradictory dates require different records. Reopen the sources to check your explanation. Record one condition under which your own verdict would need reconsideration.

text: **Manual:** `operating-manual-v1`. **Task:** Prepare and review a synthetic action-list example for the proposed thirty-minute workshop. **Authority:** Maya reviews consequential meaning under the memory charter. The project index leads to the existing learning-loop-v1 selector, which selects instructions-v3. The knowledge map provides navigation. title: Worked input and acceptable output
text: Synthetic input: S14:1 The facilitator agreed to send the revised exercise notes on Thursday. S14:2 The group agreed to ask the venue about access soon; no owner was assigned. S14:3 A reminder on Friday was suggested, but no decision was made. Action Status Owner Timing Source Send revised exercise notes Agreed Facilitator Thursday S14:1 Ask venue about access Agreed; assignment unresolved Not assigned “Soon”; exact date unspecified S14:2 Send reminder Suggested; no decision Not established Friday proposed, not confirmed S14:3 **Review:** An actual output may use different wording, but must preserve these distinctions. title: Worked interruption

title: Acceptance criteria

title: Common failure and repair

text: Each role has a stated purpose and an inspectable returned object. Current instruction and permission authority remain unchanged unless separately reviewed. title: Common failure and repair
text: Failure Repair Two files are counted as two required results. Match artifact roles and content, not only message count. Checker returns a rewritten draft without a report. Require source findings and the exact inspected candidate; keep rewrite as an optional addition. Old comparison accompanies a new candidate. Hold the join; check the new version and identify the new target. Same identity arrives with different content. Preserve ambiguity and require a clear versioned return. Source changes while roles are working. Keep attempt inputs stable; identify and review the new source version before combining results. Two roles agree without inspecting source. Derive expected properties from source and require traceable comparison. Coordinator invents substantive approval. Limit it to completeness/compatibility; route meaning to responsible review. Repair limit is bypassed by renaming the job. Preserve the job's bounded allowance and escalate remaining defects. Role separation adds work without useful evidence. Return to the simpler workflow or narrow the additional role.

text: The offer, operational evidence, and commercial hypotheses are distinguishable. Intake and scope identify the actual result and needed source/permission. Authorized reversible production proceeds without repeated ceremonial approval. Whole-deliverable review extends beyond the narrow source-check workflow. Internal readiness, actual delivery, customer acceptance, and learner effects are separate states. Human ownership of customer communication and consequential commitments is explicit. Capacity includes preparation, review, repair, maintenance, and support assumptions. Simulated work cards expose holds and next decisions without becoming market evidence. Extra diagnosis silently consumes the reserve. Record the trade-off and revise scheduling or scope. One-off accommodation becomes permanent offer policy. Preserve the decision's limited scope; review any broader change separately. Agent renames failed work to bypass the repair limit. Keep the bounded job history and return remaining defects to human diagnosis. Restored historical package overwrites later work. Rehearse separately, compare states, and preserve current authority.

title: Constructed Fieldwork case
text: Everything below is authored fiction. The three conversations, quotes, consent, proposals, pilot, feedback, acceptance, and cost figures are constructed teaching material. No real person was interviewed; no actual payment, customer validation, learner effect, or author autobiography is established. Readers must keep their own observed results separate from this example. **Record:** `product-experiment-v1`. **Starting capability:** The earlier demonstration and operating manual support practice in preparing and reviewing source-faithful action-list examples. The service remains a workshop-brief review and activity redesign, rather than a claim that an action-list extractor alone teaches people. **Hypothesis:** An independent educator with an upcoming short workshop and an unclear participant task may pay for a bounded review and redesign that produces a pack they can rehearse.

title: Three discovery scenes
text: Within the story, each educator agrees to discuss a current workshop problem and let Maya retain brief notes for this inquiry. No permission for public quotation, real learner data, external publication, or unrelated material is inferred. ID Constructed dialogue and situation Interpretation and next step D21-A Educator A: “We talk through the meeting example, but I finish without anything I can check. I need them to make an action list during the session.” Has a draft thirty-minute brief and authority to commission a small review. Relevant participant-performance gap. With permission, inspect the brief and prepare P21-A. Purchase not yet established by the statement. D21-B Educator B: “My learners already produce action lists. The difficult part is getting them to arrive prepared.” Different problem. No proposal in this experiment; do not count the conversation as agreement about A's design gap. D21-C Educator C: “I can write the activity. I want another person to check whether it fits the half hour and whether my feedback is clear.” No next workshop scheduled. Plausible review need, uncertain timing. Prepare P21-C if welcome; interest is not purchase. **Rejected summary:** “All three educators need our activity-redesign service.” **Repaired interpretation:** A describes a relevant task-design gap; B describes preparation; C describes review and timing. Only later proposals and decisions can establish willingness to commission the specific offer.

title: Two candidate proposals
text: **P21-A — Educator A:** For illustrative USD 300, review one existing thirty-minute workshop brief, redesign one activity so participants produce a source-faithful action list, and return an annotated review, revised activity, source-linked example, review criteria, facilitator sequence, and change note. Include one bounded revision round. Exclude a full course, branded slide deck, software, live facilitation, recruitment, and unlimited revisions. Use only the authorized brief and synthetic practice material. Acceptance means a pack meeting the criteria below is ready for the educator's own rehearsal; no learner improvement is promised. **P21-C — Educator C:** The same illustrative USD 300 bounded package, with diagnosis focused on timing and actionable feedback in the educator's existing activity. Scope and deliverable limits remain the same. Response: deferred because no session is scheduled. No purchase, receivable, or future revenue is recorded. **Agreed pilot:** `PP21-01`, from P21-A. Educator A agrees to the USD 300 fee and stated scope. This is one agreed paid pilot in the fiction. No invoice or payment receipt is supplied. Revenue recognition and collection must remain separately labeled in subsequent arithmetic.

title: Authorized brief constraints for PP21-01
text: B21-1: The workshop lasts thirty minutes. B21-2: Adult participants use supplied synthetic meeting notes to make an action list. B21-3: The list must distinguish agreements and suggestions, supported owners and timing, and unresolved details, with source references under the existing instructions-v3. B21-4: Participants make an individual attempt, compare it with review criteria, and revise at least one relevant part or explain why no correction is required. B21-5: The educator receives a sequence they can rehearse, an example and criteria, and the reason for consequential design changes. B21-6: Acceptance is of the reviewable pack; actual facilitation and learner outcomes are outside this pilot's observed evidence.

title: Inspectable pack components retained in PB21-v2
text: The following authored materials make the reviewable pack available for inspection. They do not report an actual facilitated session. Give participants the task and source before showing them the corrected example. **Annotated brief review:** Educator A's constructed account says participants talk through the meeting example but leave no action list to inspect. The redesign therefore makes an individual written list the central task. The brief's thirty-minute limit governs the whole sequence; PB21-v1 fails that limit and the revised agenda below repairs it. The review adds comparison against source-based criteria and a revision opportunity, so feedback can change the participant's work rather than merely confirm attendance. **Five-minute facilitator model, M21:** Use this short example before the main attempt: Status Item Owner Timing Source Agreed Send joining instructions Facilitator By Monday M1 Suggestion Add parking information Unspecified Unspecified M2 Explain why M2 remains a suggestion with gaps. Ask participants which words support the status and which details the note does not establish. This model uses a different source from the main attempt, so it does not reveal the C16 answer in advance. **Main practice source:** Use the exact five-item C16 packet, including both “by Thursday” and “by Friday” handout claims. Its deliberate uncertainty is part of the task. Do not edit the source to make the output easier. **Participant instruction:** “Read C1–C5. Individually make an action list with Status, Item, Owner, Timing, and Source columns. Preserve agreements and suggestions as stated. Keep supported timing, including deadline qualifiers; mark missing details. Where the two handout notes disagree without an established supersession, retain their shared information, show both claims, and request clarification. Cite the source lines for each item. Leave yourself room to revise after comparison.” **Blank participant output:** Status Item Owner Timing Source                     **Review criteria:** The governing rule remains instructions-v3. Compare the participant's attempt with these properties: C1 retains the slides commitment, coordinator, and “by Tuesday”; C2 remains an unassigned suggestion; C3–C4 retain the shared handout action and facilitator with both unresolved deadline claims; C5 remains an agreement with unspecified owner and timing. Every row retains its source references. Different faithful wording can pass; matching the example word for word is not required. **Worked example for the comparison stage:** Reveal the reviewed corrected C16 candidate after the individual attempt. Its references allow the educator and participant to check each choice against the source. **Source-based feedback example:** If a participant writes “Agreed: coordinator asks the library,” say: “C2 says this was suggested and nobody accepted it. Which cells would preserve that evidence?” The relevant revision is to Suggestion and Unspecified owner. Do not replace the whole response without having the participant locate and explain the discrepancy. **Revision instruction:** “Change at least one part that fails the criteria and name its source-based reason. If your attempt already meets them, explain one decision that might otherwise look incomplete, such as keeping both handout deadlines unresolved. In the closing discussion, identify the question you would need answered before assigning a single handout deadline.” **Change note:** Preserve the individual attempt and revision. PB21-v2 reduces orientation from five to three minutes, the model from eight to five, and the attempt from ten to eight; keeps comparison/revision at eight; and gives closing six rather than five minutes. The net reduction is six minutes. The educator must rehearse the sequence to see whether these allocations work with their intended participants.

I cannot fit that into the session we agreed.” **Repair decision:** Narrow the model and optional discussion while preserving the participant attempt and revision. The source-faithful example and criteria still follow the current instruction. title: Economics handoff
text: These figures are illustrative case assumptions, not actual bookkeeping: Item Figure Meaning Agreed pilot fee USD 300 One pilot; not two proposal fees and not proof of collection. Delivery 4 hours Includes initial pack and timing repair. Acquisition 2 hours Allocated across all three discovery conversations and both proposals. Support 1 hour Separate from delivery and acquisition. Owner time 7 hours Sum of the three time categories. Cash cost USD 20 Allocated experiment cost. Owner-time value for the next chapter's model USD 50/hour Assumed opportunity cost, not a measured wage or an additional cash payment. If USD 300 is treated as earned revenue in the explicit unit-economics scenario, economic contribution is `300 − 20 − (7 × 50) = −70` USD. Do not describe that scenario as a receipt or as evidence about an actual business. The internal synthetic package slots from Chapter 20 are not a delivery-time estimate for this larger pilot.

title: Decision and unresolved questions
text: Retain the accepted pack and the rejected overlong candidate. Investigate which work recurs, what could be narrowed, and whether price and scope can support sustainable delivery. Learner performance, repeat demand, market size, provider reliability, and collected cash remain unresolved or unobserved. A second identical engagement has not been agreed.

title: Acceptance criteria
text: A demonstrated capability connects to a specific buyer situation rather than a generic audience label. Discovery wording, inference, buying response, and delivery acceptance remain distinguishable. The offer states input, output, criteria, price, scope, timing, and revision boundary. A real experiment records actual consent, communication, and evidence; the fictional packet is never copied as proof of a reader's results. A delivery failure can be located against an agreed criterion, repaired, and reviewed in the revised version. Fee, revenue, cash, owner time, and learner outcomes retain their separate meanings. The next action addresses a stated remaining uncertainty, including a justified stop or narrower offer.

title: Common failures and repairs
text: Failure Repair Praise becomes an invented purchase. Record the exact response and wait for an actual agreement on the specific scope and price. Different problems become one attractive summary. Return to each account and identify its particular task, alternative, and timing. One paid pilot becomes a market-wide conversion forecast. Retain the small selected sample's limits and gather evidence appropriate to the next decision. A useful pack violates agreed duration or scope. Check the whole deliverable against the brief; repair the affected version before accepting it. Unpaid acquisition and support disappear from costs. Record those categories alongside delivery and cash. Buyer acceptance becomes a claim of learning. Obtain appropriate learner evidence in a separate future exercise; keep current outcome untested. A new delivery error changes an unrelated instruction. Locate the responsible procedure and preserve correct existing behavior.

title: Optional Economics Calculator
text: This optional companion to Chapter 22 of *Accumulated Curiosity* applies the book's planning formulas to explicit assumptions. You can complete the same exercise on paper. The calculator does not establish earned revenue, an invoice, a cash receipt, tax or bookkeeping treatment, customer demand, or achieved efficiency. Download the complete ZIP, or inspect the Python source, synthetic scenarios, standalone tests, and verification notes.

title: Start without code
text: Choose one currency and one period. Use consistent units throughout. Distinguish a unit of completed work from the whole period. Write these inputs on paper: Per-unit input Your assumption Price treated as modeled earned revenue  Attributable variable cash cost  Delivery hours, including repair  Acquisition hours allocated to a completed unit  Support hours allocated to a completed unit  Assumed value per owner hour  Period input, when modeling a month or another period Your assumption Available owner hours  Fixed operating hours  Fixed cash cost  Modeled whole-unit volume, or use calculated capacity  Then calculate: “Floor” means round down to a whole unit: 120 ÷ 7 permits 17 whole units under the assumptions, not 18. This is a capacity calculation, not a demand forecast. For a modeled period volume `n`: An equivalent cross-check is: The allowance values owner time for this planning exercise. It is not automatically a cash payment, salary, or accounting expense. The calculated cash-surplus label does not prove that revenue was collected.

title: Keep the pilot unit separate from a monthly operation
text: The fictional pilot's unit assumptions are USD 300 price, USD 20 attributable cash, four delivery hours, two acquisition hours, one support hour, and an assumed USD 50 per owner hour. The two acquisition hours already allocate work across the three discovery conversations and two proposals, including unsuccessful sales effort. Do not add that same effort again as another unit expense or inside fixed operating hours. Fixed operating hours should represent other work not already included in the unit's delivery, acquisition, or support hours. The paper calculation is: This calculation treats the price as modeled earned revenue. It does not turn the fictional agreement in Chapter 21 into evidence of payment or recognized income. The `pilot_unit` scenario intentionally has no period model, so no monthly fixed overhead is silently allocated to this one-unit illustration. A separate one-unit monthly scenario would include the chosen month's fixed overhead. It answers a different question. To see that distinction, the baseline monthly model with `--volume 1` yields 80 before the owner allowance, 47 total owner hours, and −2,270 after the allowance. It does not replace the pilot's −70 unit result.

title: Read the two monthly scenarios
text: All figures here are synthetic assumptions. The proposed price and reduced delivery time are unvalidated changes, not observed improvements. As in Chapter 22, interpreting the period result as a cash surplus assumes all modeled revenue is collected and the listed cash costs are paid in the same period. The calculator has no separate receipt dates or payment dates; it cannot verify that assumption. Taxes, financing, equipment purchases, owner withdrawals, and omitted costs remain outside this model. Result Baseline Proposed Price 300 750 Variable cash per unit 20 35 Delivery / acquisition / support hours 4 / 2 / 1 3 / 2 / 1 Unit owner hours 7 6 Unit contribution after USD 50/hour allowance −70 415 Available / fixed operating hours 160 / 40 160 / 40 Whole-unit capacity 17 20 Revenue at modeled capacity 5,100 15,000 Variable cash 340 700 Fixed cash 200 200 Cash surplus before owner and tax 4,560 14,100 Total owner hours, including fixed work 159 160 Owner allowance 7,950 8,000 Remainder after allowance −3,390 6,100 !Two hypothetical monthly scenarios share 160 available hours, 40 fixed operating hours, and an assumed USD 50 per owner hour. Baseline seven-hour units permit 17 units, producing 4,560 before the owner allowance and minus 3,390 afterward. Proposed six-hour units permit 20 units, producing 14,100 before the allowance and 6,100 afterward. These are planning assumptions, not demand or receipts. *The capacity calculation constrains modeled work. The owner allowance changes the interpretation of the remainder; it does not describe a verified cash payment.*

title: Run the optional script
text: Prerequisites: Python 3.9 or newer and an ordinary terminal. No packages, API keys, account connections, or network access are required. Extract the ZIP, open a terminal in its folder, and run: The `-B` option tells Python not to create bytecode cache files. The calculator itself reads the selected input file and prints to standard output or standard error; it has no save or network operation. Actual baseline output: Other useful runs: The last command prints all three supplied scenarios. Repeat `--scenario` to select several. A volume override requires exactly one selected scenario with a period model.

title: Observe an overcapacity request without hiding it
text: For the baseline with `--volume 20`, the calculator keeps the requested volume at 20. It does not silently reduce it to 17. The result includes: Field Actual result `capacity_units` 17 `modeled_volume` 20 `exceeds_capacity` true `revenue` 6000 `variable_cash` 400 `cash_surplus_before_owner_and_tax` 5400 `total_owner_hours` 180 `owner_allowance` 9000 `remainder_after_allowance` −3600 The 180 modeled owner hours exceed the 160 available. The arithmetic remains visible so that you can decide which assumption needs reconsideration. The flag does not authorize overtime, prove available demand, or resolve the conflict for you.

title: Edit a scenario deliberately
text: Keep the supplied examples intact and create your own scenario file manually. Each input document contains a three-uppercase-letter `currency` label and a `scenarios` list. The label does not convert currencies or validate an exchange rate. Each scenario requires: A period model is optional. When included, it requires: Optional `period.modeled_volume` selects a whole-unit volume. Omit it to use capacity. `--volume` overrides that field for the one selected period scenario. Omitting `period` creates a unit-only illustration; the JSON result then contains `period: null`. Use decimal strings such as `"20.25"` for easy inspection. Ordinary JSON number tokens are also read directly into `Decimal`, without first becoming binary floating-point values. Money and hour values in JSON output are exact decimal strings. Unit counts are integers and the capacity flag is a Boolean. No values are rounded to two decimal places by this model. All numeric inputs must be finite and nonnegative. The total unit owner hours must be positive. Fixed operating hours may equal, but may not exceed, available hours. Volumes must be whole numbers. Booleans are rejected wherever a number is required, even though some programming languages treat `true` as one. This is deliberately bounded teaching software: at most 100 scenarios, a regular UTF-8 input file of at most 1 MiB, up to 100 coefficient digits per number, and a stored decimal exponent between −100 and 100. Unknown or duplicate fields, duplicate scenario IDs, missing required fields, non-finite values, and malformed input produce explicit errors. There is no silent fallback to zero.

title: Inspect an error and repair its input
text: For example: Actual error: The program exits with status 2 and prints no result for invalid model input. Correct the specific field and rerun. A valid overcapacity request is different: it exits successfully and reports `exceeds_capacity: true` because its arithmetic is defined, even though its requested work exceeds the modeled capacity.

title: Check one assumption at a time
text: The tests include two independently hand-derived sensitivities: Raising only the baseline price to 450 leaves capacity at 17. Unit contribution after allowance becomes 80; period remainder is still −840 after fixed cash and all owner hours. Increasing only baseline acquisition time from two to three hours makes each unit eight hours. Capacity falls to 15; unit contribution after allowance becomes −120; period remainder becomes −4,000. These are arithmetic consequences, not recommendations or validated scenarios. If an acquisition-time figure already includes unsuccessful sales effort, count that effort once. If work exists even when no units are completed, place the relevant unallocated work in the fixed category rather than letting it disappear from the model.

title: Verify the companion
text: Run the standalone tests: They exercise the actual CLI with literal expected values, including the supplied monthly scenarios, unit-only pilot, zero volume, overcapacity, exact decimal handling, high-precision products, malformed input, booleans, and sensitivity cases. Tests create and remove temporary fixture files; they verify that the calculator leaves the tested input and working folder unchanged. The verification notes record the independent arithmetic checks and observed test result. Passing these checks establishes the tested calculations and input behavior. It does not validate the business assumptions or establish tax treatment, accounting recognition, demand, payment, or future delivery performance.

title: Acceptance and repair
text: The exercise is useful when you can explain the formulas without running the script, distinguish the unit from the period, identify which inputs are assumptions, and reproduce at least one result by hand. If the result differs from your worksheet, first check whether you included fixed owner hours, used the same modeled volume, or counted acquisition/support effort twice. If input validation fails, repair the named field. If a valid scenario exceeds capacity, change or investigate the assumption deliberately; do not remove the flag merely to make the plan look feasible.

title: Unit economics and capacity
text: Use with Chapter 22. Define the offer, record all work, and compare a baseline with a proposed change. Paper, a calculator, or an ordinary table is sufficient. The optional Python calculator automates these arithmetic relationships with synthetic inputs.

title: Blank reusable template
text: An owner-time allowance is a selected comparison value, not cash wages paid. The remainder is not a calculation of taxable profit or personal take-home income. Cash-surplus interpretations require the stated collection/payment assumption. Keep actual cash dates in a separate list if they differ.

title: Fictional worked example: Fieldwork
text: **Record:** `unit-economics-v1`. **Case source:** PP21-01 and its effort record. Three constructed discovery conversations led to two proposals and one agreed USD 300 pilot; the second proposal was deferred. The revised pack was accepted for rehearsal. No payment receipt is supplied. **Unit:** One agreed workshop-brief review, one activity redesign, and a reviewable pack with one bounded revision. This is the whole pilot package, not Chapter 20's internal forty-five-minute production slot.

text: Both original planning scenarios assume 160 available owner hours, forty fixed operating hours, USD 200 fixed cash, and USD 50 per owner hour. They assume all modeled revenue is collected and all listed cash costs are paid in the same period. Actual cash timing, taxes, financing, equipment purchases, owner withdrawals, and omitted costs are outside the model. Neither establishes demand, achieved efficiency, a sustainable schedule, actual collection, or real profit. Twenty slots are capacity under assumptions, not twenty buyers.

title: Changed cases to inspect
text: Change from proposed inputs Whole-unit capacity Modeled volume Owner hours Remainder after allowance, USD Only ten units sold/completed 20 10 100 1,950 Acquisition takes five hours per unit 13 13 157 1,245 Unused available hours receive no allowance in this simplified model. If the owner needs compensation for reserving all available hours, add that separate requirement to the decision record; do not infer it from the remainder. **Baseline capacity challenge:** Request twenty units with the original seven-hour unit. Required hours are `40 + 20 × 7 = 180`, exceeding 160 by twenty. Arithmetic at the requested volume gives USD 6,000 revenue, USD 400 variable cash, USD 5,400 cash surplus before owner/tax, USD 9,000 owner-time allowance, and **−USD 3,600** remainder. Retain those results and flag the infeasible schedule; do not silently replace twenty with seventeen.

title: Decision and next evidence
text: Do not repeat the baseline at scale on these assumptions. Investigate whether a revised scope/price addresses a buyer's actual need and whether a specific delivery change preserves the accepted criteria in less time. Keep the price conversation, delivery timing, acquisition record, and cash collection as separate evidence. A further pilot must have a stated learning question and effort limit.

title: Acceptance criteria
text: The unit matches the scoped offer and includes its support/revision obligations. Every input is labeled as observed or assumed; the fictional sample is not used as market evidence. All three effort categories and relevant fixed work are counted once. Unit and period results reproduce the displayed arithmetic. Owner-time allowance, actual compensation, cash collection, and profit are not conflated. Changed cases state which inputs changed and why the result moved. Over-capacity volume is visible; unused availability is interpreted correctly. The final action follows from a stated constraint and names the missing evidence.

title: Common failure and repair
text: **Failure:** A reader replaces the actual four delivery hours with a hoped-for one hour, calls the result measured savings, and multiplies it by every possible slot. **Repair:** Restore the original effort record. Put the proposed one-hour case in a separate column, name the process change it depends on, and test that change against the same delivery criteria. Model a separate sales volume. Until evidence exists, label the faster work and full demand as assumptions. **Failure:** A calculator gives the expected number, so the reader accepts the business plan. **Repair:** Verify one result by hand, then challenge the inputs. Correct arithmetic supports only the stated calculation. It cannot establish demand, timeliness of payment, or the usefulness of the offer.

title: Capability Portfolio
text: Use with Chapter 23. Keep one evidence table for a stated domain. The canonical level names come from the TFIS homepage; the columns and checks below are book-developed practice. This is not an official certificate, validated score, or a new maturity framework.

title: Blank reusable portfolio
text: **Portfolio ID, owner, date, and working domain:** **Current task, allowed actions, and consequential limits:** **Current instruction route and actual version:** **Relevant source/permission boundary:** **Help used: manual work, assistant, agent workflow, other reviewer:** **Next operation I want to rely on:** Level and canonical name My bounded claim and conditions Actual evidence location, version, and observation Failure or missing evidence Next useful demonstration or repair L0 Task Operator     L1 AI-Assisted Operator     L2 Workflow Orchestrator     L3 Agent Supervisor     L4 Multi-Agent Architect     L5 Sovereign Architect     Leave unsupported cells empty or write “not demonstrated.” Preserve the actual input, supplied context, first output, review, correction, and relevant repeat result behind a claim. Identify constructed examples and planned tests as such. Do not turn a supplied answer into an observed result. The Functional Life uses Manual Operator, Tool User, Workflow Builder, and Loop Engineer at L0, L1, L2, and L4 respectively; L3 and L5 share the homepage names. Its closed-feedback emphasis informs the book's verdict checks. The variants are descriptions within TFIS's sources, not additional levels.

title: Challenge one claim
text: **Claim selected and exact supporting record:** **What another reviewer could establish from that record alone:** **What required an unstated memory, missing source, or assumption:** **Revised claim:** **Demonstration needed to restore a broader claim:** **Input and expected properties prepared before the attempt:** **Actual first result, review, repair, and relevant repeat result:** **What remains unresolved:**

title: Review conditions
text: Check the existing TFIS pillars without producing a weighted score. Agency: what can proceed under the stated limits? Clarity: whose task and acceptance criteria govern? Competence: can you explain and diagnose the work? Accountability: where is the judgment, and what state was actually verified? Security: what access, permission, portability, and recovery conditions apply? **Conditions that should trigger re-review:** Changed instruction, model/setup, source format, tool permission, material task scope, or discovered defect. Identify which prior evidence each change affects.

title: Worked sample: fictional Fieldwork
text: **Portfolio:** `capability-portfolio-v1`. **Domain:** Source-faithful action-list examples and a reviewable thirty-minute workshop-design pack. The current selector reaches instructions-v3. The rationale explains its history; it is not a second selector. The records below are demonstration resources from the fictional case. They are authored teaching specimens, not actual user runs or advanced-level certificates. A reader who performs a corresponding exercise should fill the table with their own observed evidence. The portfolio does not give Maya an independently verified overall rank.

title: Evidence routes already available
text: **L0 — direct task understanding:** Start with the capability baseline, literal workshop practice set, and inquiry brief. They show what the activity is intended to elicit and how review can expose a missing performance. A reader's next evidence is an actual unaided attempt and explanation, with time and repair recorded under a consistent standard. **L1 — useful assistance:** The Chapter 7 two-pass packet supplies v1/v2, exact sources, the flawed Wednesday date, migration diagnosis, and changed-input specimen preserving “soon.” The Chapter 16 demonstration adds the case where current v3 is supplied but a suggestion is promoted into an agreement. These are distinct diagnoses. Keep actual assisted first attempts to determine which occurs in your own work; the source's suggested trial count is not a validated threshold. **L2 — connected workflow:** Use the operating manual and delegated workflow practice to inspect the sequence and handoffs. The relevant evidence is a complete observed input→extraction→candidate→source comparison→bounded repair→review packet. If the human supplies each step, record that help rather than calling it independent execution. **L3 — bounded supervision:** The delegation contract defines the permitted sequence, return, and escalation. The review policy and review practice show withdrawn acceptance and repaired review of a candidate that merged distinct objects. A policy file is a prerequisite; an actual executor's trace and the supervisor's observed response are still needed for an operational claim. **L4 — architecture and retained judgments:** The system contracts make source/candidate identity and role completeness inspectable at the join. V13-01 shows a scoped correction that must preserve both imprecise and explicitly supplied timing. A complete operational claim needs the actual architecture used, observed role handoffs, the approved stored verdict, write verification, and a later attempt that reads and applies it. The book's constructed records do not supply those runtime observations for the reader. **L5 — meaningful replacement and recovery:** The portability drill and synthetic package provide a no-code rehearsal of context reconstruction, missing input, and stale authority. The enterprise runbook adds operating capacity and recovery responsibilities. File access in another editor is distinct from observed behavior on another model/provider. The portfolio records which was actually tested, plus the dependencies that remain. **Commercial context alongside the levels:** The product experiment contains three constructed discovery conversations, two proposals, one agreed USD 300 pilot, and a revised pack accepted for rehearsal. The unit-economics model tests financial assumptions. Neither buyer agreement nor a favorable scenario proves an SSA-CMM level; no payment receipt or learner outcome is supplied by these teaching records.

title: E23-01: repair an overstated verdict claim
text: **Candidate claim:** “L4 complete: the verdict ledger is implemented and next-run improvement is verified.” **Attached material:** The Chapter 13 authored packet: Input A, bad output, V13-01, reviewed correction, Input B, and expected properties. It explains the operation but is not a receipt of an actual write or agent execution. **Revised claim:** “I can explain and rehearse scoped verdict review using this specimen. Durable write and changed-input use in my actual configured workflow remain to be demonstrated.” **Next demonstration:** Within authorized practice records, review one actual candidate, save the approved verdict to its intended location, reopen it, and follow the maintained route into a later attempt. Use a changed source that explicitly supplies a date. Inspect whether the output retains that date while respecting the earlier correction against invented precision. **What would fail:** A saved file that contains different wording; a pointer resolving to history; an alleged retrieval that cannot identify the relevant record; a new output copying the old answer or erasing the explicit date. Name which happened, repair that dependency, and repeat the affected check. Do not declare success merely because the expected behavior is described here.

title: E23-02: narrow an unsupported provider claim
text: **Candidate claim:** “Provider independence passed.” **Attached material:** A record of opening the selected Markdown working set in another location/editor. No second-provider output is included. **Revised claim:** “Selected files are readable and their context can be reconstructed under the recorded local conditions. Provider behavior remains untested.” **Next demonstration if relevant:** Supply only authorized task/source material to an available different assistant, retain the exact configuration information you can observe, and run both the precision/uncertainty and conflict cases. Keep the answer key separate until review. Record any adaptations. A substantive instruction change creates a different procedure whose earlier cases need appropriate rechecking. **No second provider available:** Keep the narrower claim and continue the useful local recovery practice. The exercise does not require purchasing access or inventing a comparison.

title: Historical-version inspection
text: Follow run-02, then the current selector. The specimen belongs to v2; current main-case work uses v3. A valid historical link does not make the specimen a test of a version it did not use. Preserve the historical record and ask for a fresh current-version observation before making the broader execution claim.

title: Acceptance criteria
text: A bounded domain, task, help used, and current authority are explicit. Claims link to actual evidence, and constructed resources remain distinguishable from observed performance. An input, supplied version, first output, review, repair, and relevant repeat can be inspected where the claim depends on them. Manual rehearsal alone is not described as deployed agent supervision, multi-agent coordination, verified runtime learning, or provider interchangeability. The five pillars expose specific gaps without hiding them in a numerical average. One defensible claim and one corrected overstatement lead to an appropriate next demonstration. A change in conditions triggers review of the affected claim without rewriting valid history. Commercial assumptions, income, and capability claims retain their separate meanings.

title: Common failures and repairs
text: Failure Repair Every row contains a confident label but no observation. Narrow the claims, link actual evidence, and mark the remaining demonstrations unperformed. The portfolio contains only polished final answers. Retain first attempts, the assistance used, consequential corrections, and their reviewed scope. An old test is labeled a pass for the current configuration. Restore its actual version; test the changed configuration when the claim requires it. A saved verdict is treated as proof it guided later work. Inspect the stored state, subsequent retrieval, changed-input output, and review separately. Two drafts are presented as independent drafting and checking. Require the actual role outputs and matching source/candidate references before the join. Provider behavior is inferred from readable files. Retain the access result and mark model behavior untested until it is actually observed. Revenue is used to claim operational maturity. Inspect the system behavior and business economics as separate evidence. The next gap becomes a project to automate everything. Choose the missing condition that blocks the next useful authorized operation.

title: Solo Enterprise Plan
text: Use with Chapter 24. Connect a defined economic direction with the evidence, capacity, dependencies, and next decisions needed to pursue it. This is an original planning exercise, not a forecast, a new maturity framework, or a promise of income.

Do not hide their work or costs. **Economic direction:** Gross annual revenue / profit under a stated definition / owner income / valuation. Choose and define the primary metric, currency, and period. **Why this direction serves the work and life I want:** **Current buyer situation and offer:** **Evidence available now:** Link actual capability demonstrations, discovery, agreements, delivery review, payment status, and outcome observations. title: Worked example: fictional Fieldwork
text: **Plan:** `solo-enterprise-plan-v1`. The entire Fieldwork case is fictional. Its existing commercial events and all figures below are authored illustrations. The ninety-day actions are proposed future work, not completed events. No real customer, payment receipt, measured learner outcome, achieved annual revenue, company valuation, or advanced operational certification is supplied.

title: Starting state
text: The product experiment contains three constructed discovery conversations, two proposals, and one agreed USD 300 pilot, PP21-01. Its PB21-v1 pack exceeded the thirty-minute brief; PB21-v2 repaired the agenda and was accepted for the educator's own rehearsal. No second sale is agreed. The capability portfolio preserves which demonstrations a real operator must still perform. **Economic direction being investigated:** USD 1 million in gross annual revenue. Profit, owner income, collected cash, and valuation remain separate. This target is not a forecast or an outcome of the single pilot.

title: Exact illustrative unit assumptions
text: Assumption Baseline pilot model Proposed alternative Unit price/revenue assumption USD 300 USD 750 Unit cash cost USD 20 USD 35 Delivery, including repair 4 hours 3 hours Acquisition, including unsuccessful proposals 2 hours 2 hours Support 1 hour 1 hour Total owner time per unit 7 hours 6 hours Owner-time value USD 50/hour USD 50/hour The baseline's USD 300 was the agreed fee; treating it as earned revenue is the explicit unit-economics scenario. Collection is not observed. The USD 750 price, demand, cash cost, and six-hour efficiency are proposed assumptions, not verified improvements. Baseline unit economic contribution: `300 − 20 − (7 × 50) = −70` USD.

title: Monthly capacity and economics
text: Both scenarios assume 160 available owner hours per month, forty fixed operating hours, 120 remaining unit hours, and USD 200 fixed monthly cash cost. The owner-time allowance is not an additional cash payment in the cash-remainder row. As in Chapter 22, these monthly cash remainders assume all modeled revenue is collected and the listed cash costs are paid in the same period; no collection is observed in the pilot. Result under the stated assumptions Baseline Proposed alternative Whole-unit capacity 17 20 Unit hours used 119 120 Total owner hours, including fixed work 159 160 Revenue if all units sell and are earned USD 5,100 USD 15,000 Unit cash costs USD 340 USD 700 Fixed cash costs USD 200 USD 200 Cash remainder before owner compensation and tax USD 4,560 USD 14,100 Owner-time allowance USD 7,950 USD 8,000 Economic contribution after that allowance −USD 3,390 USD 6,100 Neither row set supplies a buyer pipeline. The proposed month uses every modeled owner hour, with no additional contingency reserve. An actual commitment can be lower; record the chosen reserve and recalculate the result instead of counting reserved time as sold capacity.

title: Annual target and the constraint it reveals
text: Twenty units × USD 750 × twelve identical fully sold months = USD 180,000 annualized revenue. Twelve such months are assumed, not forecast. At USD 750, reaching at least USD 1 million in annual gross revenue requires 1,334 whole units, producing USD 1,000,500. Proposed annual capacity is only 240 units. At six owner hours each, the target would require 8,004 unit hours before fixed operations. The current design cannot supply that volume within the stated time allocation. **Implication:** A different useful product or operating arrangement is needed to change the sales-to-owner-work relation. Additional agents do not create customers or eliminate human work merely because they can produce drafts concurrently.

title: Constructed planning mistake and repair
text: **Mistake:** “The higher-price scenario has positive contribution, so this is now a million-dollar plan.” **Repair:** Keep the positive modeled contribution conditional, then calculate annualized revenue and whole-unit capacity. Record the remaining demand, price, effort, and capacity questions. Do not label the proposed alternative validated or make commitments using a buyer count the record does not contain. **Second mistake:** Counting the USD 14,100 cash remainder as disposable owner income while ignoring the owner-time requirement, obligations, collection timing, and tax exclusion. **Repair:** Keep the exact metric label. Establish actual cash and obligations separately, and use the explicit owner-time allowance for the economic comparison rather than subtracting it twice as cash.

title: Selected first route and alternatives
text: **Initial proposed route:** Continue investigating a bounded workshop-review and activity-redesign service. Examine a narrower reusable pack before promising a broader product or more volume. This is a proposed next experiment, not another agreed engagement. **Educational alternative:** Test whether an educator can use a reusable pack with the described support. Purchaser acceptance and participant learning need separate evidence. Record support and maintenance rather than assuming digital delivery removes them. **Software alternative:** Test a valuable interaction first, then automate a stable operation with inspectable source handling, authority, failure behavior, and recovery. Account for ongoing technical and support work. Do not build software solely to bypass unresolved demand. **Current operating boundary:** `learning-loop-v1` still selects `instructions-v3`; no v4 is created here. The runbook, review policy, verdict practice, and portability drill guide operation. Customer communication and consequential commitments remain with the human unless separately authorized. Earlier forty-five-minute internal simulation slots are not pilot delivery estimates.

title: Proposed ninety-day sequence
text: Period Working question Evidence-producing work Continue, change, or stop Days 1–30 What does the current offer require, and whose current problem fits it? Inspect the existing pilot/brief, retain actual delivery/acquisition/support observations in a real exercise, and hold bounded consented discovery with relevant people. Update scope and costs using inspected material. Narrow unclear scope or return to capability work before taking further commitments. Mark all unknown demand and payment states explicitly. Days 31–60 Does one proposed redesign retain useful quality at workable effort and price? Test one changed scope or delivery arrangement. If proposing USD 750, record the actual buyer response. Keep first output, review, repair, and total effort. Retain only assumptions supported by the new evidence. If quality or effort fails, revise or stop the particular redesign rather than expanding volume. Days 61–90 Which part deserves repetition, and can the intended operation be recovered? Compare relevant repeated work; inspect support variation; perform needed current-version, missing-source, or provider/collaborator handoff checks. Recalculate costs and capacity. Choose a defensible offer and commitment level; keep uncertain operations manual or pending. Record remaining dependencies and the next review trigger. These periods organize proposed work. For actual use, name the material, counterparties, resource budget, and permitted actions in your plan, then retain your own results rather than treating the example sequence as completed work.

title: Constraints and review conditions
text: Do not promise more work than the chosen capacity and reserve permit. Keep a source-dependent delivery pending if necessary evidence cannot be inspected. Revisit scope or price when actual acquisition, delivery, or support contradicts the model. Record whether a payment is agreed, earned under the stated treatment, invoiced, or collected; do not spend an assumed receipt in the model. Keep source-faithfulness and the learner's individual attempt/revision when redesigning the pack; a faster output with missing essential work is a different result. Reassess the route if the relevant buyers do not choose the defined offer. Interest is not a sale. Include the work and cost of any collaborator openly. Team choices follow the purpose and evidence, not the need to defend a label. Protect a stated allocation for maintenance, recovery, and exploration within the actual time budget.

title: Acceptance criteria
text: The primary economic metric, currency, period, and motivation are clear. Current evidence and future assumptions remain distinct. Price, units, cash cost, owner time, fixed work, demand, and whole-unit capacity are connected by correct arithmetic. Annualization is conditional, and a target is not reported as a forecast or outcome. The selected operating route states what must change and which new dependencies it creates. The ninety-day plan yields reviewable records and decisions, with conditions for stopping or changing course. Human judgment, authority, collaborator needs, and recovery remain explicit. The plan can be explained without AI and revised when its assumptions fail.

title: Common failures and repairs
text: Failure Repair Revenue, profit, cash, owner income, and valuation share one label. Define the metric and preserve the costs, period, and collection state relevant to it. A fully sold month is multiplied into a forecast. Label the annualization and inspect demand, capacity, variation, and time off separately. A higher price or lower delivery time becomes an accomplished improvement. Keep it proposed until a relevant buying/delivery test supplies evidence. Owner work disappears because an agent did the first draft. Count acquisition, review, correction, support, and fixed operations in the appropriate categories. Every modeled hour is promised without acknowledging variation. Choose an operating reserve or lower commitment and recalculate the economics. A new product form inherits the old cost assumptions. Inspect its actual support, maintenance, delivery, and distribution work. “Solo” hides outside labor or excludes needed expertise. State the ownership model and include collaborators' roles, costs, and authority. The plan allows only expansion. Write evidence-based conditions for narrowing, choosing another route, or stopping.

title: Calculator verification
text: Checked on September 10, 2026, using Python 3.11.3. The program is a standard-library teaching model intended for Python 3.9 or newer. This is a report of the checks performed, not a claim that every operating system or input has been tested.

title: Behavior checks
text: The supplied `test_economic_scenarios.py` contains 19 standalone test methods. They run the real command-line program with synthetic JSON files and check returned results and errors. Expected numbers are literal independently calculated values; the tests do not import the calculator's arithmetic to generate their expectations. The tests were written before the calculator. The first run failed because the production program did not yet exist. After implementation, the observed result was: The checks cover: the baseline, proposed, and separate pilot-unit calculations; requested volume above capacity remaining unclamped and flagged; a JSON volume setting and an explicit command-line override; zero volume retaining fixed costs and fixed operating hours; zero remaining unit capacity; exact decimal fractions and products beyond Decimal's default precision; JSON numeric decimals avoiding binary-float conversion; price and acquisition-hour sensitivity; rejection of booleans in numeric fields, negative/nonfinite/nonnumeric numbers, excessive numeric bounds, zero unit hours, excessive fixed hours, and fractional volume; duplicate, missing, unknown, or malformed fields, duplicate scenario IDs, invalid JSON, missing files, unknown scenario selectors, and invalid volume overrides; readable output distinguishing a unit-only illustration from a period and reporting overcapacity; unchanged input-file bytes and unchanged working-directory contents across a calculator run. Run them from the extracted folder with: The test runner creates and removes temporary synthetic fixture files. The calculator itself only reads its selected file and prints results or errors. Source inspection found no network or file-save operations in the calculator. The read-only observation is bounded to the tested runs; it is not a security certification of Python or the host computer.

title: Document and visual checks
text: The companion guide was compared with Chapter 22's formulas, actual command-line options, field names, and output. It states the same-period collection/payment assumption required to interpret the period cash-surplus label. It does not assert that an agreed pilot fee was collected. The original SVG was rendered locally and visually inspected. Both monthly comparisons separate capacity, cash before the owner allowance, and the remainder after valuing all working hours. Text alternatives describe the values and their limits. A long label that approached the panel boundary was split into two lines before the final inspection.

title: Interpretation limits
text: Correct arithmetic does not establish demand, achieved efficiency, a sustainable workload, a payment, or a financial reporting conclusion. This model assumes constant per-unit costs and effort, separately supplied fixed costs and hours, one currency, whole-unit volume, and the reader's chosen hourly allowance. It does not infer taxes, financing, equipment costs, owner withdrawals, cash timing, market price, or omitted work.
